newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-GOITSCHEL WINS GOLD 30 YEARS AFTER RACE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GOITSCHEL WINS GOLD 30 YEARS AFTER RACE.

text.p: Thirty years after finishing second in the Portillo world championship downhill behind a winner later declared a man, Marielle Goitschel was officially presented with the gold medal on Saturday.
The Frenchwoman, now 51, is now the only woman in modern times to have won world championship gold in all the Alpine skiing disciplines. She won nine medals in all.

Goitschel received the medal from International Ski Federation (FIS) president Marc Hodler at a ceremony in her home town of Val d'Isere marking the 30th anniversary of the world championships in Chile.
"I'm very moved to be able to wear this medal officially after having received it eight years ago from Eric Schinegger, who really made a remarkable gesture," she said.
In the Portillo downhill, Goitschel was second to Austrian Erika Schinegger, who later underwent a sex-change operation, married and became a father.
